faqs.question: What does the CA 15.3 Test measure?
faqs.answer: It measures Cancer Antigen 15-3 levels in blood to support monitoring of breast cancer treatment response, progression, and recurrence.

faqs.question: Do I need to fast before this test?
Can the CA 15.3 Test detect breast cancer early?
faqs.answer: No. It is not a screening test and is primarily used for monitoring in patients with known breast cancer.

faqs.question: What does a high CA 15.3 level mean?
faqs.answer: It may suggest recurrence or metastasis in breast cancer, but it can also rise in benign conditions; clinical correlation and further testing are needed.

faqs.question: Can men take the CA 15.3 Test?
faqs.answer: Yes. Although commonly used in breast cancer monitoring, CA 15-3 may be elevated in other cancers as well.

faqs.question: How soon will I get my CA 15.3 report?
faqs.answer: Reports are typically available within 8 hours after the sample is received by the lab (may vary by location).

faqs.question: Which method is used for this test?
faqs.answer: The test is commonly performed using Electrochemiluminescence Immunoassay (ECLIA).
